timed_text.text: Day 18.
The biggest reason athletes break: they've never planned for the worst.
Not the success, the worst case.
What happens if you fall behind early?
What if you make a visible error in front of the biggest crowd ever?
What if your body gives out before the competition is over?
Most athletes avoid those questions.
They think planning for failure invites it.
That's backwards.
Planning for adversity makes you dangerous — response ready in advance.
This is the then plan.
If X happens, then I do Y.
It's not pessimism, it's preparation.
Research is clear on this.
Pre-planning adversity: you recover faster and perform more consistently.
You're not hoping the bad thing doesn't happen.
You're deciding in advance that it doesn't own you.
On screen — build your If-Then plan for three likely adversity scenarios.

cards.prompt: What is the most likely thing to go wrong in your next competition — the one that typically starts your mental spiral? Describe the scenario and write your exact response: breath, reset word, refocus.
Second most likely adversity scenario — and your response.

timed_text.text: You just made three decisions in advance.
When those moments arrive and they will, your brain already has the answer.
No freeze, no spiral, just a plan.
Now that you're finished, day 18 is complete.
